engagement_title: Sterling Row channel package: bring eight mixed light penthouse stills to one prestige white point, recover the lobby wordmark off a brass plaque, cut a restrained opening film and its vertical, and carry the whole thing onto an editable end card and a printed residence card for every unit
vertical: Real Estate, Construction and Property. A single broker's video channel selling nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, starting just over 4 million dollars, to ultra high net worth buyers.
real_brief_anchor: Adapted from a real Upwork post in which a top producing luxury real estate broker running an online video channel (market insight pieces plus property walkthroughs, three or four a month) asks for a per video content package: a click worthy on brand thumbnail that is explicitly NOT a generic headshot with a text box, a cinematic cold open teaser that is cross postable as a square, and a consistent branded end card, all with luxury brand restraint and a 48 to 72 hour turnaround. The real post named no company, so the brokerage is laundered to the coined fictional wordmark Sterling Row and the broker stays an unnamed figure. REASONABLY ENRICHED into the fuller commission that client genuinely needed rather than three assets per video: the reason every video looks like a different person made it is that the source photography was never brought to one look, so the engagement leads with the eight mixed light hero stills; the reason the end card cannot simply be typeset is that the only surviving version of the wordmark is a photograph of a brass plaque in the lobby; and the same nine residences need a printed card each off the developer's existing spec sheet. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest: an ink level trace off photographed printed artwork recovers a real mark, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, and a real press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly.
client_one_liner: Every video on my channel looks like a different person made it, the only copy of our wordmark that exists is a photo of the brass plaque in the lobby, and I turn these around in two days.
client_brief:
Sterling Row, channel package for the residences

Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block. They start just over four million. We sell them one at a time, to people who are not in a hurry and who have seen everything.

I run a video channel. Two market pieces and one walkthrough a month, and the channel is where most of my buyers first meet me. Right now every video looks like a different person made it, because a different person did.

What I am sending. Eight hero photographs of the residences, five from the building's architectural photographer and three my sales team took on a phone, which I only mention because you will notice. Three clips from the penthouse walkthrough. A voice track of me reading the market piece, recorded at home. A photograph of the brass wordmark in our lobby, which is the only version of it anybody can find. The developer's printed spec sheet as a PDF, and the unit list.

What I need. The eight photographs looking like one building, shot by one person, on one day. A short opening film for the channel, and a tall version of it. One cover still, and it cannot be me standing next to a window with a yellow arrow on it. An end card and a square frame I can cross post, both of which I need to be able to edit myself, because the unit and the price change every video and I turn these around in two days. And a printed card for each residence, one page each, from the spec sheet.

The restraint matters more than anything else. My buyers are not persuaded, they are reassured. Quiet, near neutral, almost no text on screen. Anything that looks like a promotion loses them, and once it looks cheap I cannot spend my way back.

Please tell me what you changed, what type I am on, and what I should know about the wordmark.
price_band_and_audience: Full floor residences from just over 4 million dollars, sold to ultra high net worth buyers who are typically buying their third or fourth property and who are reassured rather than persuaded. The band is load bearing in a specific direction: at this tier the grade sits near neutral and slightly cool with clean whites and no crushed blacks, motion is slow and largely static, on screen text is minimal and small, and the wordmark reproduces at a size that would look timid on any other listing. Ship the same material with a saturated warm grade, fast cuts, large benefit captions and a price burned across the frame and it reads as a mass market development, and a UHNW buyer reads that as a building that is struggling to sell, which is precisely the impression that ends a 4 million dollar conversation. Push the other way into pure atmosphere with no unit information at all and the broker loses the qualified buyer who needs to know which floor and how many square feet before she will ask for a viewing. A posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,500 dollars fixed, on a 48 to 72 hour cycle.

brand_identity.sector: Luxury residential: full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, sold through a single broker's video channel.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, a converted warehouse block of nine full floor residences, sold one at a time through one broker's channel of three or four videos a month.
brand_identity.about: Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, starting just over four million dollars, sold to buyers who are not in a hurry and have seen everything. The channel is where most buyers first meet the broker, so every piece has to feel made by one hand. Restraint is the whole proposition: these buyers are reassured, not persuaded.
brand_identity.audience: Ultra high net worth buyers, typically on their third or fourth property, reassured by evidence and calm rather than by benefit claims, who still need the floor, the square footage and the exposure before they ask to view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Full floor residences from just over four million dollars, the top of the market. Presentation sits near neutral and deliberately small: anything that looks like a promotion reads, at this tier, as a building that is struggling to sell.
brand_identity.typography: One reassuring, near neutral pairing that avoids both extremes: no high contrast display serif that reads as a perfume advert, no heavy grotesque that reads as a development brochure. Text sits small and calm, the wordmark reproduces modestly, on screen copy is minimal by rule.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, composed, confident without pressure. Example: "Nine residences. Full floor. Sold one at a time, to buyers in no hurry."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only surviving version of the wordmark is a handheld photograph of the cast brass plaque mounted in the lobby, lit from one side. There is no vector file and no clean scan. The developer's spec sheet exists only as a printed PDF, and the disclosure wording is fixed and cannot be changed.
brand_identity.values: Discretion and accuracy. The developer's restraint rules and disclosure lines are contractual, and the brand is protected by never looking like it is selling.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_residence_stills/ (8 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Hero photographs of the residences, five from the building's architectural photographer and three taken by the sales team on a phone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Eight hero rooms. Five are the photographer's and three are ours, which you will notice."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three sales team frames are substantially smaller than the channel's cover specification, so a cover cut from one of them reaches size only by interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a hard cap while reporting it solely inside its own returned tradeoffs and never in a message or a warning. Separately two of the photographer's frames were lit tungsten against blue hour glass, so no single white point serves both the room and the window: correcting the room takes the city outside green, and correcting the window takes the room grey.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_walkthrough/ (3 clips)
assets_supplied.kind: Penthouse walkthrough footage, two clips from the photographer's cinema body and one handheld pass shot by the broker.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Three clips from the penthouse. One of them is mine, handheld."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The handheld pass is at a much lower capture size than the other two and it carries the only footage of the terrace, which is the single thing UHNW buyers ask about first. Because re aspecting and resizing never add pixels, any vertical teaser that includes the terrace is ceilinged by that one clip rather than by the two good ones, and the ceiling is not visible from the clip in isolation.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_lobby_plaque.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the cast brass Sterling Row wordmark mounted on a dark stone lobby wall, lit from one side.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of our wordmark anybody can find. It is on the wall in the lobby."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Brass on dark stone runs close in value across the lit half of the plaque, and it is a disjoint wordmark on a photographed substrate rather than a flat scan. A prompt naming the plaque returns the plaque rather than the letters, background removal on lettering keeps only a fragment or two because subject detection needs one coherent blob, and the resulting trace looks clean and open at canvas size while its counters behave differently at the size the mark actually reproduces on a near black end card.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_broker_read.wav
assets_supplied.kind: Voice track of the broker reading the market insight piece, recorded at home.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Me reading the market piece. Recorded at my kitchen table."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: There is a hard reflective room under the read and a refrigerator compressor that cycles on partway through, so the tail of the track sits in a different acoustic space from the head. Speech enhancement lifts the voice and reduces the hum, but the room change remains audible as a shift in space rather than as noise, which is exactly the kind of thing a UHNW viewer registers as amateur without being able to name it.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_spec_sheet.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The developer's existing printed unit spec sheet, one residence per sheet, supplied as the template for the printed card run.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The developer's spec sheet. We want a card per residence off this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sheet prints as a clean grid of separated blocks, but the frame granularity the conversion exposes bears little relation to the printed page, and one residence's price line is longer than the fixed measure it lands in. A fixed frame does not spill and does not flag: it stops rendering, so that record comes out cut mid figure while the merge reports success and the page count is exactly right.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_units.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Nine residences: unit designation, floor, square feet, exposure, ceiling height, outdoor space, price, availability.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The nine residences. Two are already under contract and should say so."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Per record raster proofs from a multi record run come back in an order that does not match their labels, so proofs named by their position in the response are attached to the wrong residences. On a nine unit run that means a proof sheet in which the broker signs off a price against a unit that does not have it, and nothing in the response indicates the mismatch.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_brand_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the developer: the restraint rules, the approved descriptive language, and the two disclosure lines required on printed material.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The developer's rules. The disclosure wording is fixed."

acceptance_bar: The eight hero stills read as one building photographed by one person on one day when laid in a row the way a channel banner lays them: one white point, one black point, one treatment of glass against interior light.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. A cover that reaches the channel's size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The cover still is not a person beside a window with a graphic pointing at it, and it would not embarrass a buyer who forwards it to her advisor.
The opening film and its vertical are both restrained: slow, largely static, near neutral, and the vertical's honest ceiling is stated rather than asserted.
The broker's read sits in one acoustic space across the whole piece, or the shift is named in the note rather than shipped hoping nobody hears it.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it still reads as the wordmark at the size it actually reproduces on the end card ground rather than at canvas size.
The end card and the square frame are live editable text and live vector in a working file the broker can change himself, not a picture of a layout.
All three authored canvases are in one working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the self contained source it was built from is delivered alongside.
The residence run is one page per unit for all nine, every field present, nothing truncated at the measure, both disclosure lines on every page, and the two units under contract marked as such.
Every per record proof is attached to the residence it actually depicts. A proof sheet in which a price sits against the wrong unit fails outright at this price band.
One type system across the end card, the square frame and the printed cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states, per photograph and per clip, what was applied and why, every resize any tool reported, what the terrace footage ceilings, and everything the broker should know about using the recovered wordmark.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster and trace decision in the commission. It fixes one prestige white point from the strongest photographer frame and brings all eight toward it one call at a time, confines corrections where a room and its blue hour window cannot both be served globally, cuts the cover without ever enlarging past what the sales team's phone actually captured, and recovers the wordmark at ink level off a photographed brass plaque with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

The opening film and its vertical. Summarisation finds the two or three beats in three walkthrough clips that carry a full floor residence, speech enhancement takes the kitchen room off the broker's read, the highlight cut shortens the assembly into a restrained opening (it only ever shortens), and the re aspect derives the vertical without adding a pixel, which is what makes the terrace clip's capture size a real limit on what the vertical can show.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The channel package as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes: the end card, the square cross post frame and the vertical title card. This is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout, the wordmark goes in as inline vector so it stays editable, every photograph must be inlined as image data because a referenced photograph renders as an empty grey box at full success, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carrying the end card, the square frame and the printed residence cards. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land as reassurance rather than as luxury signalling, which at this tier is a real and easy mistake. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a weight, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the face falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (including its validator mode), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed residence card run off the developer's own spec sheet, one record per page across all nine units, plus the press PDF and per record proofs the broker signs off. This surface is where a fixed measure decides whether a long price line survives to trim, where per record raster output has to be produced by a route whose record identity is guaranteed rather than inferred from response order, and where verification means reading the document rather than believing the success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame nobody has, an exterior context band for the opening film, because the developer's own building exteriors are under embargo until closing. IP clean, at genuine camera scale, with generative results excluded. The Boards half is genuinely load bearing on a 48 to 72 hour cycle with a broker who travels: it persists the selects he approves from, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The end card and square frame must be editable every video, which puts them on the authoring surface; the residence cards are one record per page at volume, which is the one thing the merge surface is for. Both destinations are pinned by the brief, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export later.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: The manifest has to record each still's and each clip's capture size beside its role, because those numbers bound the cover and the vertical and the client has not mentioned them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role, with capture sizes recorded.

trajectory.action: Look at all eight stills and all three clips: which stills are the photographer's and which are the phone's, which stills are lit tungsten against blue hour glass, which clip carries the terrace, and what each one's capture size actually is.
trajectory.judgement: The broker volunteers that three stills are his team's, but not that they are too small for the cover, and not that the terrace lives only on the handheld clip. Both facts decide what can be promised, and neither is legible from the pictures alone.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering capture size, illuminant, mixed light frames and what each clip uniquely contains.

trajectory.action: Summarise the three walkthrough clips to find the beats that carry a full floor residence, then enhance the broker's read.
trajectory.judgement: At this tier two or three held beats do more than twelve. Enhancement takes the kitchen room and the compressor off the read, but the change of acoustic space partway through is a different problem and has to be listened for rather than assumed handled.
trajectory.produces: A beat list with reasons, a cleaned voice track, and a written note on where the room changes.

trajectory.action: Cut the opening film to the beat list, pacing it slow and largely static.
trajectory.judgement: The cut is where the price band becomes visible. Restraint here is not an absence of decisions: choosing which two beats carry the building, and refusing the third, is the decision.
trajectory.produces: The landscape opening film with a written cut rationale.

trajectory.action: Derive the vertical teaser from the master and state its honest ceiling.
trajectory.judgement: Re aspecting never adds pixels, so a vertical that includes the terrace is bounded by the handheld clip. The choice is whether the terrace is worth the ceiling or whether the vertical does without the one thing buyers ask about.
trajectory.produces: The vertical teaser plus a written statement of what bounded it and what was traded.

trajectory.action: Level what is off level, then fix one prestige white point from the strongest photographer frame and bring each of the eight toward it with its own call.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good rooms. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames from two cameras under different light, and near neutral at this tier means near neutral rather than cold.
trajectory.produces: Eight graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine the corrections on the two mixed light frames, selecting the material by its own visual properties rather than by the room it sits in.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the room pulls the selection to the room. Serving the interior and the blue hour city through one global move is not possible, and choosing which one leads is an art direction call, not a technical one.
trajectory.produces: Two frames where the room and the window both sit correctly, with the parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the cover still at the channel's specification, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The brief bans the headshot with an arrow, so the cover has to earn a click on composition alone. The crop tool will interpolate up to a hard cap while reporting it solely inside its own tradeoffs, and three of the eight candidates are below the target size to begin with.
trajectory.produces: The cover still with its tradeoff record transcribed, cut from a frame that did not need enlarging.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the exterior context band, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then look at it beside the graded eight.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the prestige target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame, and a judgement about whether it belongs.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and place the graded set, the cover candidate and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap.
trajectory.judgement: The broker travels and the cycle is two days, so the board is the sign off mechanism rather than a nicety. A partial response is partial, and only the entries it names as failed are re sent.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the brass plaque: an ink level selection naming the letterforms' own visual properties, the correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the brass letters and not the plaque or the stone, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or a colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on disjoint lettering entirely.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark with its hygiene done.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, and composition
trajectory.action: Place the recovered wordmark at the size it will actually reproduce on the end card, on the near black ground the end card actually uses, and look at it there rather than at canvas size.
trajectory.judgement: A mark is judged at reproduction size on its real ground or it is not judged. At this tier the wordmark sits small, which is the condition under which a trace is least forgiving.
trajectory.produces: A reproduction size proof of the wordmark on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against reassurance rather than luxury signalling: a high contrast display serif at this tier reads as a perfume advertisement, and a heavy grotesque reads as a development marketing brochure. A weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the end card, the square cross post frame and the vertical title card at three canvas sizes, place the wordmark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, inline every photograph as image data, declare family and weight on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A referenced photograph is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how little can be on screen and still tell a qualified buyer which residence this is.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole channel package, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every normalisation this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable, and a restrained treatment has fewer elements, so a single missing one is the whole canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Convert the spec sheet PDF, export the document structure and read what the conversion actually exposed, build the mapping from the document's own reconstructed story text, prepare the template, then round trip it and confirm every expected field is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: The printed sheet's clean grid says nothing about the frame granularity a conversion produces, and the placeholder step reports success while silently dropping mappings. Verification has to read the document, not the response.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template with every field confirmed present, or a named list of the ones that did not land.

trajectory.surface: InDesign layout and data merge, and handover
trajectory.action: Merge all nine residences one record per page by a route whose record identity is guaranteed rather than inferred, proof every page, render the press PDF and the per record proofs, then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: A fixed measure does not spill, it stops, so the long price line truncates while the page count stays exactly right. Per record raster output cannot be named by its position in the response, so identity has to come from a route that guarantees it. The note has to be specific enough that the broker's next editor does not repeat the archaeology on the wordmark.
trajectory.produces: A nine page press PDF, correctly identified per record proofs, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed exterior frame actually belongs beside the eight graded residences. Before licensing, the only readout available is a small thumbnail plus the frame's true dimensions and whether it was generated, and at thumbnail scale a blue hour exterior reads as neutral. Its real illuminant, its grain structure and how its whites sit only exist once the full resolution file is downloaded and placed adjacent to the eight stills that have already been brought to the prestige white point. It can look plainly bought while every individual property of it looks fine, and no amount of study of the thumbnail predicts it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the frame cannot be graded, cannot be judged against the set, and cannot even be seen at real scale until it has been licensed and pulled down, and there is no preview channel between the thumbnail and the licensed file. (b) Nothing states it: the brief never mentions Stock at all, and the acceptance line about the eight reading as one building is the client's own requirement, not a warning about a purchased frame. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is either a second license against a different candidate, which costs real time inside a 48 to 72 hour cycle, or abandoning the purchased context band and re planning the opening film's first beat around footage the broker owns.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Judge the licensed frame beside the graded eight rather than alone, and if it cannot be brought without breaking its own sky, license a different candidate or re cut the opening beat from owned material, then re grade whichever frame survives to the same prestige target and re place it on the board.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An opening film whose first frame is visibly a stock photograph sitting next to eight photographs of the actual building, on a channel whose entire selling proposition to a UHNW buyer is that nothing here is generic.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered wordmark survives at the size it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking clean and correct at canvas size, with open counters and separated letterforms, and every response reports success. On a near black end card ground at the small reproduction size this tier demands, the counters of the enclosed letterforms close and the strokes thicken into each other, so the wordmark stops reading as words and reads as a bar. Which letterforms do this is a property of how the brass sat against the stone in that one photograph and of how the trace resolved the lit half, and it is invisible at any scale other than the real one on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the tracing tool takes no options at all, so every lever is upstream in the raster preparation, and the only way to learn whether the result holds is to place it at reproduction size on the actual ground and look. Doing it right first time would require knowing in advance how a photographed brass mark resolves, which nothing reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the plaque is the only surviving version and asks to be told anything worth knowing about the wordmark, which is a request for a report, not a disclosure of a defect. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different upstream chain, a differently worded ink level selection or a colour accurate knockout plate rather than a two colour trace, and possibly a different reproduction size and ground for the end card.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re word the ink level selection to take the letterforms rather than the lit brass field, re run the polarity and bounds decisions, re trace, re do the viewBox and background path hygiene, then re proof at reproduction size on the real ground, and if it still will not hold, tell the broker plainly what the smallest usable size is and design the end card around that.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An end card on every video the channel publishes carrying a wordmark that reads as a smudged bar, delivered as the fix for the exact problem the broker hired someone to solve.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the restrained display treatment the whole package rests on. A hairline outlined capital setting over imagery is a genuine convention at this tier and the natural way to author it is stroked type with an unfilled face, and the importer discards the stroke and resolves the unfilled face to fully transparent, so the type is present in the document, occupies its position, and is completely invisible on the canvas, at full success with no warning. Blend modes used to sit the wordmark into the dusk frame are dropped to a plain opaque shape by the same silent path. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports any of it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the square cross post frame and the vertical title card can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of that surface, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible restrained treatments survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for restraint and almost no text on screen, which is art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different typographic construction entirely, a filled face at reduced opacity or a hairline rule drawn as vector geometry, and the canvas then has to be re composed around whichever one holds.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the display treatment as a construct the importer keeps, re author all three canvases around it, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion, which are still, which need an authored fixed canvas document and which need a genuine record per page run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which two or three beats out of three walkthrough clips carry a full floor residence, and which beat to refuse, since restraint at this tier is a set of refusals rather than an absence of work.
Whether the terrace is worth the ceiling the handheld clip imposes on the vertical, or whether the vertical does without the one feature buyers ask about first.
Which of the eight frames sets the prestige white point, and how near neutral is near neutral before it reads cold and clinical rather than reassuring.
On the two mixed light frames, whether the interior leads or the blue hour window leads, since one global move cannot serve both.
Which frame can carry the cover at all, once the three sales team frames are understood to be below the target size and enlargement is not an acceptable route to it.
Selection wording on the plaque: naming the plaque takes the plaque, naming the stone takes the wall, and background removal on disjoint lettering is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which wordmark variant carries the end card, judged at reproduction size on the real ground rather than at canvas size, and what to tell the broker if neither holds small.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against reassurance rather than luxury signalling, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether a licensed exterior frame joins the world the eight residences live in or reads plainly as bought, and what to do inside a two day cycle if it does not.
Which merge route guarantees record identity for the per record proofs, given that response order cannot be trusted to name them.
How little can be on screen and still tell a qualified buyer which residence this is, where density itself is the thing that loses the buyer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns handsome pictures of a penthouse that does not exist. IDENTITY: these are nine actual residences with actual square footages, actual exposures and actual prices, and the wordmark must be RECOVERED off a photograph of the plaque bolted to the lobby wall rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different building's identity and the developer's brand rules are contractual. SPEC: nine printed residence cards, one page per unit, every field from the roster present and untruncated with two fixed disclosure lines, proofs correctly bound to the units they depict, and a cover at the channel's exact size with no interpolated pixels, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the end card and square frame are defined by being editable, since the unit and the price change every video on a two day cycle and the broker explicitly cannot re commission each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this traced mark still read small on black, did this display treatment survive the import, did this proof come back attached to the right residence.
doability_proof: Every link sits on a surface verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface carrying a gate. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale factor, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_straighten and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and the ink level trace off photographed printed artwork is verified to produce genuinely usable paths. The three checkpoints rest on documented findings rather than assumptions: crop_and_resize DOES interpolate up to a hard cap and reports it only inside its tradeoffs array; the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the fragmentary result of background removal on disjoint lettering, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and vectorize takes NO options at all so every lever is upstream, which is why a reproduction size proof on the real ground is the only test; the importer DROPS a text stroke and resolves an unfilled face to a fully transparent colour, and DROPS blend modes to a plain opaque shape, all at HTTP success with no warning, while the document rendition is documented as first artboard only, which is exactly why verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; and the Stock family exposes only a small thumbnail plus true dimensions before licensing, so adjacency to a graded set is genuinely unknowable until the full resolution file is downloaded. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, the recommender's refusal to pair is documented, and non standard numeric weights plus the slug versus PostScript name trap are live findings. MERGE: one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, per record files are producible in correct order by createSeparateFiles or a single record loop while multi record raster order is documented as unreliable, and verification by round tripping the prepared document is the documented mitigation for silently dropped mappings. PREMIERE: the video and audio calls (media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize) are submitted through the connector and their results return through the host's own progress path rather than synchronously, so this task deliberately gates NO emergent checkpoint and NO automatic verifier on a video artifact: the motion deliverables are specified by constraints the tools genuinely impose (the highlight cut only shortens, the re aspect never adds pixels) and are judged by human verifiers, while every machine checkable gate sits on the fully headless synchronous surfaces. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no compositing, no OCR, no upscaling, no per artboard export, no variable QR, no bleed claim off a converted PDF, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty.
